source: TOS13 team, 2026-10-20: the regions targeted with ACT x PONT. Framing from the ACT x PONT proposal; actors and signals are national starting points. Regional actors are for the team to add (`cloe orchestrate suggest`).

challenges.title: Circular textiles in Brabant: from waste to value
challenges.frame: Brabant as a (technology) industry and innovation region ((technologie)industrie- en innovatieregio). Reframe circular textiles from a fashion, waste or regulation issue to value: 'van afval naar waarde, van wegwerplogica naar gebruik en hergebruik, van kostenpost naar verdienvermogen'. Connect what moves in the region to national policy and European funding.

actors.name: Ministerie van Economische Zaken (EZ)
actors.interest: strategic autonomy, raw-material security and earning capacity (strategische autonomie, grondstoffenzekerheid, verdienvermogen)

actors.name: Ministerie van OCW
actors.interest: initiated PONT: using design capacity for complex societal challenges

actors.name: Actieplan Circulair Textiel (ACT)
actors.interest: a shared agenda and chain vision for the sector; facilitates those who want to act (bewaakt overkoepelende doelen, biedt een gedeelde ketenvisie)

actors.name: PONT (De Publieke Ontwerppraktijk)
actors.interest: learning how a design approach can orchestrate collaboration between governments

signals.text: No shared ownership: the issue is spread over ministries, regional governments, interest groups and companies; everyone sees the importance, nobody feels responsible for the whole.
National policy and regulation do not match what the market needs.
Circular textiles are framed as a fashion, waste or regulation issue, which brings the wrong parties to the table and asks the wrong questions.
European momentum (EU Circular Economy Action Plan, Interreg, Textile ETP), usable only when Dutch government and business go to Europe with one story.
In Brabant, governments, companies and knowledge institutions already find each other in regional chains: a starting point for national and international collaboration.
